issues.description: The template file src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java declares a public class named AnimalFarm instead of Farm, while the problem statement and the solution expect a class named Farm. This naming mismatch (and the broken/duplicated content in the template file) will prevent straightforward mapping from the specification to the starter code and cause compilation errors (public class name must match file name) or confusion when students try to implement the required Farm class.
issues.suggestedFix: Correct the template so the public class in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java is named Farm and contains the intended skeleton (or remove the malformed duplicate content). Ensure the file's public class name matches the filename and that the class signature and method stubs align with the problem statement (Farm with a List<Animal> and the required methods). This will align template, problem statement, and solution and avoid compilation and mapping confusion.
